Therefore whoever breaks one of these least commandments, and [teaches] people so, shall be called [least?] in the kingdom of heaven.
But I tell you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill; for whoever kills is liable to judgment.
But [?] whoever is angry with his brother without cause shall be liable to judgment; whoever says to his brother 'Fool' shall be liable to the council, and
You have heard that it was said: You shall not commit adultery.
For I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

Therefore, if your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into Gehenna.

And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into Gehenna.
It was said: Whoever puts away his wife, let him give her a divorce
document. But I tell you that everyone who puts away his wife, except on account of fornication, makes her commit adultery; and whoever takes a divorced wife commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not swear falsely, but you shall render to the Lord
your oath. For I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for
it is the throne of God; nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great
King. Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no'; whatever is more than these comes from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said: An eye for an eye, and [?] tooth
for [?] you: do not resist evil; but if anyone strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
And whoever wants to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
And if anyone compels you to go one mile, go
[?] two as well. Whoever asks of you, give to him; and whoever wants to borrow from you, do not turn your face away from him.
You have heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.
But I tell you: love your enemies, and bless those who curse you, and pray for those who oppress you and persecute
you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on sinners.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet your friends, what more are you doing? Do not even the gentiles do the same?
Be perfect, as your Father is perfect.
Take care not to do your good deeds before people, to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
When you do a good deed, do not proclaim it before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by people. Amen, I tell you, that is their reward.
But you, when you do good, do not let your left hand know what [your] right hand is doing,
[your right hand], so that your good deed may be in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you openly.
And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray in the synagogues and at the street corners, so that they may be noticed by people. Amen, I tell you, that is their reward.
But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you openly.
And when you pray, do not use many words like the hypocrites, for they think that they will be heard because of their many words.
Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask
him. Pray, then, like this: Our Father, who are in heaven, holy be
your name. May your kingdom come; may your will be done, as in heaven, so also on
earth. Our everlasting bread give
us today; and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors;
and do not lead us into temptation, Lord, but deliver us from evil; for yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory forever. Amen.
For if you forgive people their sins, your heavenly Father will forgive you too.
But if you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive your sins.
And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Amen, I tell you, that is their reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father, who is in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you.
Do not store up your treasures on earth, where moth and devourer destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal.
But store up your treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor devourer destroys, and where thieves do not dig through and steal.
For wherever your treasures are, there your hearts will be also.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If your eye is [?], your whole body will
be light. If the light that is in you is darkness, then how great is that darkness!
No one can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
Therefore I tell you: do not worry about yourselves, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your bodies ... [?]
[?] ... within [your own] eye you ... [?]
Hypocrite, first take that beam out of your own eye, and then you will see to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before swine, lest they turn and tear you apart.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Or which man among you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake?
If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him?
Whatever you wish people to do to you, do the same to them, for this is the law and the prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many go in
by it. For narrow is the gate and hard is the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
By their fruits you will know them. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?

And Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector, James son of Alphaeus, and Zebedee [?], who was called

These twelve Jesus sent out, commanding them and saying: "Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans,
but go rather to the lost sheep of the house
of Israel. As you go, preach and say that the kingdom
of heaven has drawn near. Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You have received without payment; give without payment.
Do not take gold, nor silver, nor bronze in your belts,
nor a bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff, for the worker is worthy of his food.
Whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy [?] until you leave.
And when you enter a house, greet it and say: 'Peace to this house.'
And if that house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
But whoever does not receive you or listen to your words, when you leave that house or city, shake off the dust
of your feet. Amen, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
Beware of people, for they will hand you over to the council and flog you in their synagogues.
And they will bring you before judges and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
But when they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you will say. [?] it will be given to you [?]

[?] hated by all because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.

But when they persecute you in this city [?]; and if they persecute you there too, flee to the next. Amen, I tell you, you will not finish going through the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple is not greater than his teacher, nor a servant greater than his master.
It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and the servant like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call the members of his household so!
So do not be afraid of them, for nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing secret that will not become known.
What I tell you in the dark, speak in the light; and what you hear in your ears, proclaim on the rooftops.
And do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies but cannot kill your souls. Rather, fear him who has power to destroy souls together with bodies in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for one penny? Yet not one of them falls to the ground without your Father.
And all the hairs of your head are counted
So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven.
But whoever denies me before people, I too will deny before my Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
For I have been sent to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a wife against her mother-in-law.
And a person's enemies will be the members of his own household.
Whoever loves his father or his mother more than me is not worthy of me; and whoever loves his son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

For this is the one of whom it is written: 'Behold, I send my angel before you, who will prepare your ways before your face.'
Amen, I tell you, there has not arisen among those born of women anyone greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

Come to me, all you who are weary and who carry heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is sweet and my burden is light.

And all the people were amazed and said, "Can this be the Son of David?"
But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, "This man casts out demons only by Beelzebul, [?] the prince of demons."
Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts and said to them, "Every kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and every city or house that is divided against itself will not stand.
And if the devil casts out devils, he is divided against himself; how then is his kingdom firm?
And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by what do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves [shall be] your judges
and they will be [?]. If I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Or how can anyone enter the house of a strong man and carry off his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And only then
will he plunder his house. Whoever is not with me is my enemy, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven to people, but the one who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this world nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; for the tree is known by its fruit.
You brood of vipers, you cannot speak good things, for you are wicked; for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good man brings forth good out of his good treasure, and the evil [?] brings forth evil out of the evil [?].
But I tell you, for every idle word that people speak, they will give account of it on that day
of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned."

Then they understood that he had not told them to beware of leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a donkey's millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depth of the sea.
Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.
If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life lame or maimed than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and enter the Gehenna of fire.
Take care that you do not despise one of these little ones. I tell you that their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountain and go and search for the one that went astray?
And if he finds it, amen, I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety [?] that had not gone astray.
So it is not the will of my Father in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between me and you alone. If he listens to you, you have gained a brother
of yours. If he does not listen to you, take one or two others with you, so that every word may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If he does not listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he does not listen even to the church, let him be to you as a tax collector and a sinner.
Amen, I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Again, amen, I tell you, if two of you agree on earth about any matter whatever they ask, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven.
For wherever two or three are gathered together for my name's sake, behold, I am there among them.
